unresolvedReferences.description: 許子將 is Xu Shao's courtesy name; the translation renders it as Xu Shao.
Pei Songzhi's chronology (Tang Heng died Yanxi 7 when Yu was two) supports a birth year near AD 163.
Gaozu and Guangwu are named only in s0022 in English; s0024 English uses possessive phrases.
趙盪寇/稚長 is rendered 'Zhao Yan' in English; standard sources identify the Dangkou general with courtesy Zhichang as Zhao Rong. Left as one person without a confirmed personal name.
The Wenshi zhuan author is written 張衡 here; kept as written and distinct from Mi Heng.
Wei Dan (Zhongjiang) is inferred to be Wei Duan's son from Kong Rong's 'two pearls from an old clam'.
典阜/營丘 allude to the fiefs of the Duke of Zhou and Taigong Wang, who are not named; no person rows created.
Two different men named Xun Yun 荀惲 appear: Xun Hong's grandnephew (courtesy Jingwen, s0137) and Xun Yu's eldest son (s0143). Kept as separate people.
先帝 in Cao Cao's memorial is taken as Han Gaozu (the hunting-dog metaphor about Xiao He); identification inferred.
Xun Yu died at fifty in Jian'an 17 (AD 212), consistent with birth ~163; the Wei shi chunqiu poison story is recorded separately as commentary.
司空 'Minister of Works' here refers to Cao Cao.
Two Xun Yi: 顗 (son of Xun Yu, Jingqian) and 霬 (grandson, son of Xun Yun); kept distinct.
Two Xun Yu besides the chapter subject: 寓 (Jingbo, son of Hou) and 羽 (son of 寓); kept distinct.
Bozi's 'present' office is dated to Pei Songzhi's time (Yuanjia, from the packet's Liu Song reign table); bounded by the packet's Yuanjia interval 424-453.
Xun Yu 昱 (the Elder, Boxiu) is distinct from Xun Yu 彧.
The Book of Wei's version of Xun You's release (persuading Dong Zhuo) conflicts with the main text (Zhuo's death); both kept.
Baima/Guandu dated AD 200 (Jian'an 5) from external era table; chunk text gives no year here.
Founding of the Wei state taken as on or after AD 213 (external; inferred).
Xun You died Jian'an 19 (AD 214) at 58 per Book of Wei; Pei computes he was six years older than Xun Yu.
Xun Biao's father is not named; recorded only as Xun You's grandson (ancestor-of, generation 2).
Dates for Li Jue's regime (AD 192-196) come from the external era table; text gives none here except Jian'an 14 for Duan Wei's death.
Weinan campaign dated AD 211 from external standard chronology; text gives no year.
Zhang Xiu's surrender dated only as before/around Guandu (on or after 199) from context.
Jia Xu's death year is not given; bounded after Cao Pi's accession (external AD 220).
陸議 is Lu Xun's original name; English renders it Lu Xun.
